headline: High: Aider’s shared git writes plus caveman’s MCP/file-based content flow create default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes repo files and shares state via a git repo, so attacker-controlled content in files can influence its prompts. caveman uses MCP and touches CLAUDE.md/project notes, creating a plausible bridge where instructions can flow through shared files. This is not proven by direct interaction evidence, so I rate it medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or notes directory, file content can be interpreted as instructions.
IF caveman writes prompt-like text into CLAUDE.md or project notes, Aider may ingest it during repo edits.
mitigations: Restrict both agents to separate repos or branches.
Add a human review step before either agent reads shared instruction files.
Disable MCP access for caveman in shared workspaces.
Use a denylist for instruction-bearing filenames like CLAUDE.md in Aider workflows.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for agent-authored file content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider has broad network egress and handles model-provider API keys, while caveman touches session logs, memory files, and project notes. If they share a workspace, sensitive code or notes can be exposed through Aider’s outbound API calls. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default use, but not directly evidenced, so medium fits.
conditions: IF the two agents share a workspace containing secrets, Aider can transmit those contents to configured model providers.
IF caveman stores memory files or project notes in the same repo, those files can be read by Aider and included in prompts or outputs.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared repos and notes directories.
Run Aider with a scrubbed workspace containing only non-sensitive files.
Separate API-key-bearing environments from shared project folders.
Review outbound prompts before sending when sensitive files are present.
requires-engineering: enforce file-level redaction before model calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider can write the filesystem and modify git state, and its shared state is explicitly via a shared git repo. caveman also operates on files and supports multiple instances. Concurrent edits to the same repo can overwrite each other or corrupt git history without locking, which is a default-dangerous conflict pathway.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same git repository concurrently, commits and working-tree changes can conflict.
IF neither orchestrator provides locking, one agent can overwrite the other's changes or create merge churn.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch.
Pause one agent while the other writes.
Use git locks or a single-writer policy.
Review and merge changes manually after each agent run.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider produces code changes and git commits, while caveman consumes project notes and supports multiple downstream writing surfaces. If caveman treats Aider’s outputs as authoritative, an error can propagate into notes or instructions. The pair lacks direct evidence of automated action-taking, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF caveman ingests Aider-generated code summaries or commit messages without verification, mistakes can be copied into notes.
IF Aider’s generated edits are later reused as source material for caveman outputs, errors can cascade across work products.
mitigations: Require manual verification of Aider outputs before reuse.
Keep generated summaries separate from authoritative notes.
Add a checklist for factual claims before caveman publishes text.
Limit Aider to draft-only changes until reviewed.
requires-engineering: add citation/traceability checks between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Aider is open-source and runs locally as the user, while caveman is also open-source with no requested elevated privileges or OAuth scopes. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a small compliance gap is visible from the documented data classes and retention-like surfaces.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into caveman session logs or memory files, local handling policies may still need review.
IF Aider is configured to send code to third-party model providers, organizational data-handling rules may apply.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared notes or logs.
Confirm provider contracts for any outbound model calls.
Document retention expectations for session logs.
Use separate workspaces for regulated and non-regulated projects.
requires-engineering: add policy-based data classification controls.
